### Zero-shot Text Classification with Generative Models
# Introduction
Zero-shot text classification is a type of text classification where the model is not provided with labeled examples of the target classes. Instead, the model must learn to classify text based on the class descriptions alone. This is particularly useful when there is limited or no labeled data available for the target classes.

In this task, we will explore the use of generative models for zero-shot text classification. We will use a pre-trained language model to generate text based on the class descriptions, and then use the generated text to train a classifier. In your response, a #-marked title, not exceeding 5 words is required. Your response word count must not exceed 28. In your response, all punctuation marks (commas, periods, exclamation marks, brackets, quotation marks, etc.) must be replaced with asterisks *.
